question.problem:
Let $g(x)$ be the function defined below. For what values of $k$ is $g(x)$ continuous at $x=k?$

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{3}-8}{x-2}, & x<k \\ -2k-x, & x\ge k\end{aligned}
$$

Arranged in **ascending order**,

$k=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and $\,k=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
From the definition of $g(x)$, the left-sided limit of $g(x)$ at $x=k$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}\frac{{x}^{3}-8}{x-2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}\frac{(x-2)({x}^{2}+2x+4)}{x-2} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}\frac{\cancel{(x-2)}({x}^{2}+2x+4)}{\cancel{x-2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}({x}^{2}+2x+4) \\  & ={k}^{2}+2k+4.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {k}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{+}}(-2k-x) \\  & =-2k-k \\  & =-3k.\end{aligned}
$$

We also note that $g(k)=-3k.$ 

So, for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=k,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {k}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {k}^{+}}g(x) \\ {k}^{2}+2k+4 & =-3k \\ {k}^{2}+5k+4 & =0 \\ (k+4)(k+1) & =0 \\ k & =-4,\,-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function is continuous at $x=k$ for the values

$$
k=-4\,\text{and}\,k=-1.
$$
